title: Poly-symptomatology of chronic multi-canalicular benign paroxysmal positional vertigo: a deductive, inductive, and abductive narrative review
authors: Carsten Tjell; Wenche Iglebekk; Peter Borenstein
fulltext_exclusion_reason: fewer than two domains substantively covered
pain_condition_detail: chronic multi-canalicular benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (mc-BPPV) in patients with vestibular migraine, whiplash associated disorders, and other chronic pain disorders
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses 'biopsychosocial' as a label for conditions lacking objective findings, contrasting it with organic vestibular pathology. It does not define the model, integrate domains, or operationalize any BPS constructs. The review is a neurophysiological account of mc-BPPV symptoms.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper asserts that vestibular reflexes cause cognitive dysfunction, but no pathway is specified. No social domain integration.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper uses 'biopsychosocial' as a label for conditions lacking objective findings, yet provides a purely biological (vestibular) explanation for all symptoms, creating a tension between the label and the content
conceptual_tensions_2: The paper argues that mc-BPPV symptoms are often misdiagnosed as biopsychosocial, implying BPS is a diagnosis of exclusion, not an integrative model
additional_observations_1: The paper is a narrative review of mc-BPPV symptomatology from a neurophysiological perspective, not a review of chronic pain. It uses BPS language only to contrast with organic vestibular pathology
additional_observations_2: The review uses a tripartite classification (deductive, inductive, abductive) to grade evidence for symptom attribution, which is a novel methodological approach but not related to BPS integration
synthesis_note: This paper uses 'biopsychosocial' as a pejorative label for conditions lacking objective findings, while providing a purely biological (vestibular neurophysiology) account of all symptoms. No psychological or social content is developed. The BPS label does no explanatory work and is not operationalized.
coding_rationale: Typology is pseudo_bps because BPS language is used but only biological domain is elaborated. Triadic integration is none because social domain is absent and psychological is minimal. Bio-dominant balance reflects the paper's neurophysiological focus.

citation: Tjell et al. (2025), Frontiers in Neurology
title: Poly-symptomatology of chronic multi-canalicular benign paroxysmal positional vertigo: a deductive, inductive, and abductive narrative review
authors: Carsten Tjell; Wenche Iglebekk; Peter Borenstein
pain_condition_detail: Chronic multi-canalicular benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (mc-BPPV), with symptoms overlapping vestibular migraine, WAD, ME/CFS, and other chronic pain disorders.
bps_function_set: background framing; critique or problematization; rhetorical label
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper operationalizes chronic mc-BPPV through vestibular anatomy, otolith/cupula mechanisms, vestibular nuclei reflexes, and symptom frequencies. The BPS label is not operationalized as measured domains.
integration_mechanism_summary: Vestibular-to-neural reflex pathways are proposed for cognitive, postural, neck, and other symptoms; no biological-psychological-social mechanism is proposed.
pain_conditions_1: chronic multi-canalicular benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (mc-bppv)
emergent_labels_1: chronic multi-canalicular benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (mc-BPPV)
conceptual_tensions_1: The article treats BPPV as benign and paroxysmal while focusing on chronic multi-canalicular presentations
conceptual_tensions_2: The BPS label is used to critique misclassification, but the review's own causal account is vestibular-biological
conceptual_tensions_3: Many symptom links are deductive, inductive, or abductive, with abductive sections relying on personal experience and uncertainty
conceptual_tensions_4: Symptoms overlap with vestibular migraine, ME/CFS, WAD, and Menière's disease, making attribution difficult
conceptual_tensions_5: The review narrows objective findings to vestibular findings rather than treating lack of findings as lack of findings generally
additional_observations_1: The paper's evidence synthesis method is deductive, inductive, and abductive rather than a BPS domain matrix
additional_observations_2: The Dizziness Handicap Inventory is the only named patient-reported outcome instrument
additional_observations_3: Psychological content is limited to cognitive/affective states, anxiety, stress, frustration, and quality of life
additional_observations_4: Social content is limited to diagnosis, clinicians, physiotherapy clinics, and multiple specialists
additional_observations_5: The BPS label appears only in the abstract and introduction
additional_observations_6: The review does not report a formal risk-of-bias or quality assessment tool for included studies
synthesis_note: This review uses BPS language to argue that chronic mc-BPPV symptoms are mislabeled psychosocial when vestibular findings are absent. Its operational content is vestibular neurophysiology and symptom attribution; psychological and social material is incidental. It does not develop a three-domain model or mechanism.
coding_rationale: BPS is explicit but undefined and only rhetorical/critical. Biology dominates; psych/social are thin. Triadic integration is partial because diagnostic context and affective responses are present but not mechanistically linked.

title: Poly-symptomatology of chronic multi-canalicular benign paroxysmal positional vertigo: a deductive, inductive, and abductive narrative review
authors: Carsten Tjell; Wenche Iglebekk; Peter Borenstein
pain_condition_detail: chronic multi-canalicular benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (mc-BPPV)
bps_operationalization_summary: The BPS label is used to frame the diagnostic challenge of mc-BPPV when objective findings are absent, positioning it as an alternative to psychological disorder diagnosis rather than an integrative framework.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes that vestibular abnormalities in mc-BPPV cause downstream symptoms through specific neural pathways: vestibulo-thalamo-cortical activity leads to cognitive dysfunction, trigeminal activation causes TMJ pain, non-classical auditory pathways produce tinnitus, and vestibulo-thalamo-hypothalamic activity contributes to fatigue.
pain_conditions_1: chronic multi-canalicular benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between BPS diagnostic framing and complete absence of social domain content
conceptual_tensions_2: BPS label used to position mc-BPPV as alternative to psychological disorder, but no actual psychological constructs integrated
additional_observations_1: The review uses a tripartite classification (deductive, inductive, abductive) to grade symptom relationships to mc-BPPV
additional_observations_2: Symptoms are categorized by strength of evidence rather than theoretical integration
additional_observations_3: The paper explicitly questions whether anterior SCC involvement can be iatrogenic from Brandt-Daroff exercises
synthesis_note: This review uses the BPS label to frame mc-BPPV as a diagnostic consideration when objective findings are absent, but provides no social domain content. Biological mechanisms are well-developed, showing how vestibular dysfunction causes downstream symptoms via specific neural pathways. Psychological content is minimal, limited to cognitive symptoms linked to vestibular-thalamo-cortical activity. The BPS label functions as background framing rather than an integrative framework.
coding_rationale: BPS typology is multifactorial due to elaborated biological content and minimal psychological content with no social domain. Integration is directional bio-psych via specific neural pathways, not mechanistic triadic integration. BPS label serves as diagnostic framing, not analytical framework.
